text:
Samir: seeing a p95 jump to ~420ms in eu-central (~+2.7x baseline) starting ~02:15 UTC. throughput steady but latency tail and a small uptick in retransmits. graph: https://graphs.internal/redwood/eu-central/p95 :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Anjali: ack, can you paste the minimal query (service + model) and an example span id?
Samir: Model: redwood-v2-small, route: /generate, span: span_0x9f3a; example root request id 01AF9. Quick tcpdump around that request shows repeated ICMP fragmentation-needed from 185.9.22.0/24 -> our egress IP.
Kevin: that prefix is one of ISP-A's edge blocks. ISP-A recently pushed qos changes (policing MTU/DF flaps) in that metro. Could cause packet loss on long payloads => kernel falls back to safer (non-simd) attention kernel which increases per-token cpu and pushes batch heuristics to lower agg.
Marta: any sign of KV cache misses? if kernel slows, warmups might be delayed and we get cold-start-like behavior.
Samir: yes, noticed KV hit rate dropped ~8% across the POP at 02:14. heatmap attached (small image). also saw more small tails from worker 12 where io_wait jumped.
Kevin: profiling snippet from the offending host (short):
```
# perf top -p 2345
  29.0%  runtime/kernel_non_simd
  15.3%  attention_fastpath_avx
  12.1%  grpc_poll
  8.4%   kv_cache_lookup
```
Kernel selection logs show frequent toggles: kernel_selector: candidate=avx score=0.62 -> fallback non_simd score=0.31 (loss>0.03) repeatedly.
Anjali: so network-induced packet drops -> kernel selector oscillation -> smaller batches -> lower KV cache locality -> p95 spike. sounds plausible. can we confirm by disabling kernel oscillation or pinning kernel?
Kevin: yes. plan: temporarily pin kernel to avx for eu-central POP (override flag) and increase batching min_tokens for that POP to avoid underwhelming batch sizes. also add MTU/DF metric to the POP health checks to detect ICMP frag signals earlier.
Ops-Bot: deploy request created: deploy/override-kernel/eu-central by Kevin. CI green. rolling to 8 hosts now.
SRE-Oncall: applying route workaround too? we should avoid ISP-A path if we can steer.
Marta: I created a quick kv-warmup job to replay hottest prefixes at lower qps to restore hit-rate faster: job id warmup-206234. Starting now with 50 rps.
Samir: after kernel pin + warmup, p95 back to ~120ms within 5m. re-checking retransmits now.
Anjali: great. follow-ups: 1) add ICMP-frag -> health alert, 2) add kernel-selector hysteresis (0.05 -> 0.1) to reduce oscillation, 3) perf-eval on pinned vs auto after 24h, 4) contact ISP-A for QoS change.
Kevin: recording a micropostmortem in the incident board. short notes and diff for kernel-config are in the ticket.
Marta: leaving the warmup job running for 2 hours and will scale down.
Samir: closing thread for now, will reopen if p95 creeps again. thanks all :thumbsup:
